title: A morphism is determined on a neighbourhood by its map on local rings, and a local map of local rings is realized by a morphism, in four standard situations

standard_prerequisites.name: A subring of a local ring contains the localization of the subring at an element outside the maximal ideal, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element g outside the relevant prime over which the two maps agree, and later the element over which a map from the base into the local ring factors.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of finite presentation, and the description of a localization as a filtered colimit, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the given local map from a finitely presented algebra be realized, after localizing the source at one element, by an honest algebra map, which is what produces the required morphism in the first case of part (2).

core_obligations: Prove (1): replace the three schemes by affine open neighbourhoods of the three points, so that the statement becomes the algebra problem of two algebra maps B to A that agree after localizing at a prime, and conclude in each of the four cases that they agree after inverting one element outside that prime, either by controlling finitely many generators when the base map is of finite type or by placing a localization of A inside the local ring when A is a domain, Noetherian, or reduced with finitely many minimal primes (proof lines 10368-10390).

Prove (2): again replace the schemes by affine opens, write the given local map as a map of local rings, and in the finite presentation case factor it through a localization of the source at one element by the colimit description of localization, obtaining a morphism with the required map on local rings; in the remaining cases choose the images of finitely many algebra generators inside the local ring, localize so that the source maps into the image of the base in the local ring, and use the subring lemma to find the required localization (proof lines 10392-10421).
proof_roadmap: Reduce both parts to affine algebra problems, handle the finite presentation or finite type case by finitely many generators or by a colimit factorization, and handle the remaining cases (integral, locally Noetherian, reduced with finitely many components) by finding one localization of the target inside its local ring (proof lines 10368-10421).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a morphism is determined near a point by its map on local rings, and conversely that a local map of local rings is realized by a morphism, in four listed situations for each part (statement lines 10338-10366). The counted proof, 55 lines, proves both parts: it first reduces to an algebra problem on affine open neighbourhoods, then separates the case where the algebra structure map is of finite type or finitely presented, treated by finitely many generators or by factoring through a localization via the colimit description of localizations, from the remaining cases, treated by showing that some localization of the target sits inside its local ring and invoking the algebra lemma on subrings of local rings (proof lines 10368-10421). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof contains explicit reductions and a genuine case analysis with checkable constructions rather than restatements or bare citations, and neither part of the statement is left unproved.
